title: Finding the Sweet Spot: Optimal Data Augmentation Ratio for Imbalanced Credit Scoring Using ADASYN
summary: The paper studies how much synthetic oversampling is optimal for imbalanced credit scoring, using the Give Me Some Credit dataset (97,243 observations, 7.07% defaults) and XGBoost with SMOTE, BorderlineSMOTE, and ADASYN at 1x, 2x, and 3x multipliers. It evaluates 10 augmentation scenarios on a held-out 29,173-observation real test set, using AUC/Gini and 1,000-iteration bootstrap tests. The headline result is that ADASYN 1x is best with test AUC 0.6778 and Gini 0.3557 versus baseline AUC 0.6727/Gini 0.3453 (p=0.017), while higher multipliers degrade performance.

match_target.why: C1 is the paper's headline result: ADASYN 1x test AUC 0.6778 versus baseline 0.6727. Reproducing this single augmented run demonstrates the central sweet-spot finding without the full 10-scenario grid or bootstrap analysis.

tolerance.why: Rule 2: AUC is printed as a fraction on a 29,173-example held-out test set (2,000+ examples), so use 0.01 absolute. This prescribed band is wider than the paper's 0.0052 reported AUC gain.

requirements.stmt: Use the Give Me Some Credit dataset and binary target SeriousDlqin2yrs; after cleaning the paper expects 97,243 observations with 6 predictors and a 7.07% default rate.
requirements.quote: the cleaned dataset comprises 97,243 observations with six predictor variables and a binary target variable indicating serious delinquency

requirements.stmt: Define the positive class as SeriousDlqin2yrs = 1, i.e. serious delinquency of 90+ days past due within a two-year window.
requirements.quote: binary target variable indicating serious delinquency (90+ days past due) within a two-year window.

requirements.stmt: Use exactly the six listed predictors: age, MonthlyIncome, DebtRatio, NumberOfDependents, NumberOfOpenCreditLinesAndLoans, NumberRealEstateLoansOrLines.
requirements.quote: The feature set includes six variables spanning demographic, financial, and credit history dimensions:

requirements.stmt: Apply the stated domain caps, including age in [21, 85] years and MonthlyIncome capped at $25,000.
requirements.quote: age is bounded to [21, 85] years based on demographic data, while monthly income is capped at $25,000 to exclude extreme outliers.

requirements.stmt: After synthetic generation, round the three discrete count variables back to realistic integer values.
requirements.quote: Three variables (NumberOfDependents, NumberOfOpenCreditLinesAndLoans, NumberRealEstateLoansOrLines) are discrete integers, requiring post-generation rounding to maintain realistic values.

requirements.stmt: Use a stratified 70/30 train-test split with 68,070 training rows (4,810 defaults) and 29,173 test rows (2,061 defaults), keeping the test set untouched.
requirements.quote: We employ a stratified 70-30 split, yielding 68,070 training observations (4,810 defaults, 7.07%) and 29,173 test observations (2,061 defaults, 7.06%).

requirements.stmt: Fit StandardScaler on the training set only and transform both train and test sets.
requirements.quote: All features undergo standardization (mu = 0, sigma = 1) using StandardScaler fit exclusively on the training set to prevent data leakage.

requirements.stmt: Generate synthetic samples only in the training set after the split; never augment the test set.
requirements.quote: Synthetic generation occurs exclusively on the training set after the train-test split. The test set (29,173 observations) remains 100% real data

requirements.stmt: Implement ADASYN with kNN majority-neighbor ratios r_i, normalized weights, total synthetic budget G, and SMOTE-style interpolation.
requirements.quote: ADASYN adaptively allocates more synthetic samples to minority instances surrounded by majority neighbors (high ri), indicating regions where the model struggles to learn minority patterns.

requirements.stmt: Implement ADASYN 1x as the paper describes, doubling the minority class from 4,810 to 9,620; record any deviation from Table 1's N=72,817.
requirements.quote: Doubling the minority class (from 4,810 to 9,620 samples) yields maximum improvement of +0.0052 AUC (+0.77%).

requirements.stmt: Train XGBoost with max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.1, n_estimators=100, and eval_metric='auc' in every experiment.
requirements.quote: All experiments use identical XGBoost configurations to isolate the effect of augmentation strategies.

requirements.stmt: Set scale_pos_weight dynamically to n_majority/n_minority for each augmented training set.
requirements.quote: scale pos weight: Dynamically calculated as nmajority/nminority for each augmented training set to balance internal gradient updates

requirements.stmt: Report AUC-ROC and Gini = 2*AUC - 1 on the held-out real test set.
Use 1,000 bootstrap resamples with replacement on the test set for p-values and percentile 95% CIs.
requirements.quote: Generate 1,000 bootstrap samples by randomly resampling the test set with replacement

requirements.stmt: Set random_state=42 for the split, synthetic generation, and model training.
requirements.quote: All random processes (train-test split, synthetic generation, model training) use random state=42 to guarantee exact reproducibility.
